root.name: Mikenas Defense: Lithuanian Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nc6 2. c4 e5 3. d5 Nce7

overview: Mikenas's 1.d4 Nc6 2.c4 e5 3.d5 Nce7 is an offbeat defence in which Black's knight retreats to e7 and White gets a big space advantage with e4 and Nc3. Black's pieces are somewhat tangled and the position looks like a King's Indian or Old Indian with Black short of space. It is a rare sideline and seldom played at a high level.

white_ideas.idea: Build a pawn centre with e4, Nc3 and Nf3, using the space advantage to cramp Black
Castle and prepare f4 or a queenside break against the awkward knights

black_ideas.idea: Reroute with ...Ng6, ...d6 and ...f5 to get counterplay on the kingside
Prepare ...c6 or ...f5 to undermine the d5/e4 centre

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d5/e4 against Black e5 and d6, a locked centre with space for White

character.notes: Black is cramped and passive; White has an easy game. Balanced in the sense of no sharp play.

soundness.notes: Passive and dubious for Black; White gets an easy edge with natural moves.

structure.notes: The central pawns lock on d5/e4 against e5 and play shifts to the wings: Closed.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play it; offbeat.

level.notes: Easy for White to play; Black struggles with a cramped game. Intermediate.

character.reason: No sharp tactics but Black is cramped; a slow, passive defence.

soundness.reason: Black ends up cramped and White gets an easy edge.

structure.reason: The d5/e4 vs e5 chain locks the centre.

level.reason: Easy for White; hard for Black to get right.

plans.reason: White gets space in the centre with d5 and e4.
